value.rationale: Stochastic signal transport across feedforward networks is sensitive to observation lag and to variance accumulated from noise introduced at each site. Exact unique lag and a sharp detectability transition, with scaling coefficients and critical window, quantify a structurally motivated observable beyond the usual nonnormal variance amplification. No speculative downstream theorem is needed for this quantitative law.
